question: Should OpenClaw treat ambiguous outbound rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter as persistent pending recoverable work once the no-op deferral pacing bug is fixed?
rationale: That choice changes upgrade/runtime behavior for existing delivery queues and balances duplicate-message avoidance against stranded pending entries, which is a product policy decision rather than a pure implementation detail.

options.title: Accept pending recoverability after pacing fix
options.body: Merge the policy only after no-reconciler deferrals bypass replay pacing/deadline cost and tests prove newer replayable rows are not starved.

options.title: Keep current terminal failure behavior
options.body: Reject this PR direction and continue moving no-reconciler ambiguous rows to failed until adapter reconciliation or UI/operator recovery is designed.

options.title: Narrow to approved channel paths
options.body: Limit persistent pending behavior to channels with an explicit reconciler or planned operator surface, leaving other ambiguous rows terminal for now.

recommendation.title: Accept pending recoverability after pacing fix
recommendation.body: Merge the policy only after no-reconciler deferrals bypass replay pacing/deadline cost and tests prove newer replayable rows are not starved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits on the durable outbound delivery lifecycle and recovery queue policy that Peter has repeatedly shaped in current history.
